0.x: Background, aim and social base
**Why:** Brahmins were about **3%** of the Madras Presidency population but held **over 90%** of government jobs.

**Aim:** to further the interests of **non-Brahmins** – end Brahmin dominance in jobs, education, politics and religion; basically an **anti-Brahmin party** – "the first political party in India founded against Brahmins".
**Agenda of SILF:** social justice, a rightful place in services, political representation.
**Demand:** separate **communal representation** for non-Brahmins, on the lines given to Muslims by the Morley-Minto Reforms; opposed the Brahmin-dominated Congress.
**Social base:** non-Brahmin landed gentry, **intermediate landed castes** (Andhra: **Reddys, Kammas, Kapus**). Dalits built a parallel "Adi" movement.
**British view:** backed it to weaken **Home Rule**; used against Home Rule and Gandhi's movements; it **supported the British in the Second World War**.
**Andhra Mahasabha (Vijayawada, 1917)** sought reserved seats for non-Brahmins – **Ponaka Pattabhirama Reddy** and **Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary**.
Founding (1916-17)
**Founders:** **Dr T.M. Nair, P. Theagaraya Chetty, Dr C. Natesa Mudaliar**; symbol **Scales**.
**Papers:** **Justice** (English daily, edited by **T.M. Nair**); **Dravidan** (Tamil, 1917); took over the Telugu **Andhra Prakasika**.

1.x: Born **1827**, Satara; a gardener's son – **Mali community**, Maharashtra.
Title **"Mahatma"** given by **Vithalrao Krishnaji Vandekar (1888)**; called the **"Father of Indian Social Revolution"**.
**Creed:** all men have the same features and intellect – **nobody is sacred by birth**; aimed at the complete abolition of caste; against Sanskritic Hinduism.

**1848**: girls' school, **Pune**; taught by **Savitribai Phule** (Maharashtra) – **India's first woman teacher**; home for widows 1854; pioneer of widow remarriage → the Indian women's movement owes much to Phule's inspiration.
**Savitribai** headed the Samaj's women's section; worked for lower-caste girls.
